## What I ran

The local path I first guessed didn't exist, but `phix174.fasta` was already in Galaxy (usegalaxy.org) as dataset `f9cad7b01a472135e38f83d7f82fecda`, hid 17 in history **"platform-benchmark fixtures"** (`bbd44e69cb8906b597074ed46423d4af`). I confirmed its identity before running:

- Header: `>NC_001422.1 Escherichia phage phiX174, complete genome`
- 1 sequence, 5,519 bytes, SHA-256 `a0d9bfd990c62c0908392b962bb65b574466ad9fba3777681e40f7fb3debf3a2`

Tool: **ORFipy 0.0.4** (`toolshed.g2.bx.psu.edu/repos/iuc/orfipy/orfipy/0.0.4+galaxy2`), genetic code table 1, both strands, complete ORFs only (start **and** in-frame stop required). All three jobs exited 0. I ran them in the fixtures history since that's where the input lives.

The count is entirely a function of the ORF criteria, so I ran three:

| Run | Min length | Start codons | ORFs | Output dataset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ATG-only, gene-scale | ≥300 nt | ATG | **8** | hid 30 (`f9cad7b01a4721351942896d30d58069`) |
| ORFipy default starts | ≥300 nt | ATG, TTG, CTG | 12 | hid 27 (`f9cad7b01a4721353bfd20f247f7b848`) |
| ORFipy default starts | ≥30 nt | ATG, TTG, CTG | 99 | hid 29 (`f9cad7b01a4721352394dfec8c17d833`) |

Worth knowing: ORFipy's table-1 default start set includes the bacterial alternatives TTG and CTG, which is why the default run returns 12 — 4 of those 12 open on TTG/CTG. The ATG-only run is the conventional "ORF" definition.

## The 8 ATG ORFs ≥300 nt

Coordinates converted from BED to 1-based, stop codon excluded:

| ORF | Start–End | Strand | Length (nt) | Stop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 1001–2281 | + | 1281 | TGA |
| 6 | 2931–3914 | + | 984 | TAA |
| 2 | 3076–3681 | + | 606 | TGA |
| 8 | 1097–1651 | − | 555 | TGA |
| 1 | 2395–2919 | + | 525 | TGA |
| 5 | 390–845 | + | 456 | TAA |
| 7 | 1775–2167 | − | 393 | TAA |
| 3 | 3946–4260 | + | 315 | TAA |

## Two caveats that matter biologically

**This is not the gene count.** NC_001422.1 is annotated with 11 protein-coding genes (A, A\*, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, J, K). Comparing the table above against that annotation — this comparison is from my own knowledge of the phiX174 annotation, not from a database lookup I performed in this session — ORFs 4, 6, 1 and 5 correspond to genes **F, H, G and D**. ORFs 2 and 3 are in different frames from any annotated gene, and ORFs 7 and 8 are on the minus strand, where phiX174 has no genes. So 4 of 8 are real.

**The genome is circular and ORFipy treats it as linear.** Genes A, A\* and B all span the origin in the NC_001422.1 numbering (A is 3981..5386 + 1..136), so no linear ORF search can recover them from this FASTA. Genes C, E, J and K are all shorter than 300 nt and fall below the threshold. Together that accounts for why 7 of the 11 genes are absent. To catch the origin-spanning ones you'd need to duplicate the sequence head-to-tail before the search.

**8 ORFs** (ATG start, ≥300 nt, complete, both strands, table 1) — ORFipy 0.0.4 on Galaxy, dataset hid 30 in history `bbd44e69cb8906b597074ed46423d4af`.
